I am auditing an effort estimate for ticket "PDP – Wishlist Confirmation Message on Add" — i.e. show a confirmation/toast when a shopper adds an item to their wishlist from the PDP. I need to know whether this behaviour ALREADY EXISTS. Search VERY THOROUGHLY and report absolute file paths + line numbers.

Answer these:

1. **Base SFCC behaviour.** In `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`, grep for `wishlist` (case-insensitive). Specifically: does the base PDP (`pages/product-detail/index.jsx`) already show a toast/notification on successful add-to-wishlist? Find the `addItemToWishlist` / `handleAddToWishlist` handler and quote the exact toast call and its message/i18n id (e.g. `defineMessage`, `useToast`, `showToast`). Also check `pages/product-list/` and `components/product-tile/` for the same. Report exact file paths + line numbers + the message text.

2. **Zimmermann overrides.** What exists under `overrides/` related to wishlist? Grep `overrides/` for `wishlist` (case-insensitive) — components, hooks, pages, tests, stories. List every hit with absolute path. Is there a `wishlist-auth-drawer`, `useWishlist`, wishlist page override, wishlist icon/button on PDP or product tile? Note: recent commits mention `wishlist-auth-drawer` and SFCC-742 "wishlist login panel" — find those files.

3. **Toast infrastructure.** Find the toast/notification hook: `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` (does it exist as an override, or only in node_modules?). What is the base `useToast` signature and what does it render? Is there a Zimmermann-themed toast component or theme recipe (`theme/components/` or a `*.css.ts` for toast/alert)? Report paths.

4. **PDP wishlist entry point.** On the Zimmermann PDP specifically, is there a wishlist button rendered today? Check `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` and any `product-detail-options` / `ui-kits` component. If there's a "known gap" comment saying the wishlist button doesn't exist yet, quote it. (Check `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — it mentions a known-gaps list.)

5. **Does the PDP page override exist at all?** Confirm whether `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` exists and list its files, vs whether PDP is still the base node_modules version.

Be exhaustive on #1 (whether base already toasts) — that determines whether the ticket is a duplicate of existing behaviour. Do not write any files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). import React from 'react'
import {
    Alert,
    AlertIcon,
    AlertTitle,
    CloseButton,
    Spacer,
    useToast as useChakraToast
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'

/**
 * Display a toast message on the screen.
 * This is a custom hook to handle showing toasts in the app, preventing duplicate toasts and to add action elements
 * to toasts when required. It supports all props supported by Chakra toast.
 *
 * @param {string} title Message text to be displayed in toast
 * @param {string} id - id provided to the toast to avoid duplicate toast ids, use it if multiple toasts are needed
 * @param {string} status Semantic state of the toast - success | error | info | warning
 * @param {node} action Optional component to be displayed in the toast (eg. Button to allow user to perform action)
 * @param {string} position The placement of the toast on screen
 * @param {number} duration The delay before the toast hides (in milliseconds)
 */
export function useToast() {
    const toast = useChakraToast()

    return ({
        title,
        description,
        status,
        action,
        position = 'top-right',
        duration = 5000,
        variant = 'subtle',
        isClosable = true
    }) => {
        let toastConfig = {
            title,
            description,
            status,
            isClosable,
            position,
            duration,
            variant
        }

        if (action) {
            toastConfig = {
                ...toastConfig,

                render: ({onClose}) => (
                    <Alert status={status} variant="subtle" borderRadius="md" py={3} width="sm">
                        <AlertIcon />
                        <AlertTitle> {title} </AlertTitle>
                        <Spacer />
                        {action}
                        <Spacer />
                        <CloseButton onClick={onClose} />
                    </Alert>
                )
            }
        }
        toast(toastConfig)
    }
}

**Reference example:** the footer decomposition (SFCC-55 follow-up) split
`theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts across `footer/footer.css.ts` (shell),
`footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and
three `ui-kits/organisms/`/`ui-kits/molecules/` recipes — with `footerShared.ts` left
behind in `theme/components/` for the two genuinely cross-file values.

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `zimmButton.css.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.
- `zimmLink.css.ts`'s `sm` size renders at **22px** total height (4px `paddingBlock` ×2 +
  14px `lineHeight`), 2px short of the 24px target its own WCAG 2.5.8 touch-target comment
  names — confirmed by live Playwright measurement against a real rendered story, not a
  source read (SFCC-11 build, step 4.4, 2026-09-20). Same shape as the `zimmButton.css.ts`
  entry above: a real, small, currently-shipped shortfall pending UI-designer sign-off, not
  something any one consuming component should silently absorb or re-derive independently.
  `ZimmLink` at `size="small"` has at least 5 real consumers today (`footer`,
  `zimmSizeSelector`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmCartItemActions`) — fixing this
  means changing a shared atom's line-height token, with all five consumers' own blast
  radius to check deliberately, not a fix any single consuming step should make as a side
  effect of its own work.
- `typography.ts`'s `body1` textStyle carries **-0.12px** letter-spacing against a **-0.16px**
  raw Figma export value for at least one real screen (`ZimmCartEmptyState`'s placeholder
  body text, SFCC-11 build, step 4.5, 2026-09-21) — confirmed via a live DevTools
  computed-style check against the rendered story, not a source read. `body1` is a shared
  foundation-level `textStyle`, not something local to this one component — same reasoning
  as the two entries above: ship to spec as built, flag here for UI-designer sign-off, don't
  let any one consuming component unilaterally invent a fix or a new number. Blast radius not
  yet enumerated — `body1` is used widely across the app; a fix needs that audit done first.

## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

## Verdict: the behaviour exists in base, but Zimmermann **deliberately removed it** on the main PDP path

This ticket is not a straight duplicate — it is a **reversal of a documented product decision (SFCC-434)**. Detail below.

---

## 1. Base SFCC behaviour — YES, base toasts on add-to-wishlist

**PDP:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx`
- L244 `handleAddToWishlist(product, variant, quantity)`
- L266–283 success branch, exact call:
```js
onSuccess: () => {
    toast({
        title: formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, {quantity: 1}),
        status: 'success',
        action: (<Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
                {formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}</Button>)
    })
},
onError: () => { showError() }
```
- L290–299 already-in-wishlist branch: `title: formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST), status: 'info'` + same View action.

**Messages** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js`
| Line | id | defaultMessage |
|---|---|---|
| 123–126 | `global.info.added_to_wishlist` | `{quantity} {quantity, plural, one {item} other {items}} added to wishlist` |
| 128–131 | `global.info.already_in_wishlist` | `Item is already in wishlist` |
| 138–141 | `global.link.added_to_wishlist.view_wishlist` | `View` |
| 143–146 | `global.info.removed_from_wishlist` | `Item removed from wishlist` |

**PLP:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx` — L248 `addItemToWishlist`, toast at L273–283; `removeItemFromWishlist` L294, toast L316.

**product-tile:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx` — L281 `data-testid="wishlist-button"`, aria labels L286/293. **No toast of its own** — it only calls the parent's `onFavouriteToggle`; the PLP owns the toast.

---

## 2. Zimmermann overrides — substantial wishlist surface already built

**The decisive file:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`
- **L532** `handleAddToWishlist` — base copy, **toast retained** (`toast({...})` at L557, already-in at L578). Wired **only** to the set/bundle path (L1141, L1184).
- **L596** `handleAddToWishlistSilent` — **no toast at all**, only `{ onError: () => showError() }`. This is what the **standalone-product PDP** uses (L1296).
- **L590–595**, the load-bearing comment:
```
// SFCC-434 — toast-free add, used only by the header wishlist badge on the standalone-product
// path below. Jasmijn confirmed the PDP badge has no confirmation message, only the icon
// state change; `handleAddToWishlist` above keeps its toast for the set/bundle CTA button,
// which is unchanged and out of this ticket's scope. Omits the "already in wishlist" branch
// too — ProductView's own isInWishlist derivation guarantees this is only called when the
// current variant is not already wishlisted.
```
- L620 `handleRemoveFromWishlist` — also silent.

**Other wishlist files under `overrides/`:**

**Relevant commits:** `cd652edb` / `1260a163` (SFCC-434 PDP add-to-wishlist), `c240e692` / `478ee67f` (SFCC-742 wishlist login panel), `e0ba89e7` (SFCC-926 login panel fixes), `b81e14ae` (renamed badge, removed unused `ZimmAddToWishlist`).

---

## 3. Toast infrastructure — no Zimmermann override, no theme recipe

- `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` **does not exist**. Everything imports base: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast.js`.
- Base signature (L29–41): `useToast()` returns `({title, description, status, action, position = 'top-right', duration = 5000, variant = 'subtle', isClosable = true}) => void`. When `action` is passed it swaps in a custom `render` of Chakra `<Alert status variant="subtle" borderRadius="md" py={3} width="sm">` with `AlertIcon`/`AlertTitle`/action/`CloseButton` (L55–66).
- **No Zimmermann toast/alert theme recipe.** `find overrides/app/theme -iname "*toast*" -o -iname "*alert*"` returns nothing; `overrides/app/theme/components/` contains only `footerShared.ts`, `headerShared.ts`, `index.ts`, `navConstants.ts`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`. So any toast today renders **unstyled base Chakra**, not Zimmermann design.
- Explicit note on this at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` L90–91: wraps base `useToast` "rather than a new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an [override]".
- Known transform gap: `use-toast.js` ships JSX in a `.js` file that Vitest can't parse transitively — every test mocks it (`useCartMessages.test.tsx` L26–33, `product-view/index.test.tsx` L187).

---

## 4. PDP wishlist entry point — YES, a button exists today

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`
- L796 `renderWishlistToggle(intentIdSuffix)` renders `<ZimmWishlistBadge>` (L805–815) wrapped in `<ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer intentId={'pdp-header-wishlist-...'}>` (L833) for guests.
- Placed in the **product header beside the name** (L353–358 `wishlistButton` slot), fed at L1096 (`'mobile'`) and L1217 (`'desktop'`).
- Comment L186–192: "there is no separate CTA-column wishlist button anymore."
- Only toast in this file's wishlist path is the **error** one (L878 `showToast({title: API_ERROR_MESSAGE, status: 'error'})`), asserted by the test at L821–842.

**The known-gap comment you asked about is stale.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` L254–258:
> - The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
>   picker, **a wishlist button**, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
>   accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
>   without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.

No `product-detail-options` / `ProductDetailOptions` component exists anywhere under `overrides/` — SFCC-434 delivered the wishlist button through `product-view` instead. Worth correcting.

---

## 5. PDP override — YES, it exists

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`
```

           environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx(+stories)

```
Note `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` L265–266 flags this directory as claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md` (draft, scope still settling).

---

## Bottom line for the estimate

1. The toast **exists and works** for **sets and bundles** on the Zimmermann PDP (`handleAddToWishlist`, L532).
2. For **standalone products — the common case — it was deliberately stripped** in SFCC-434 with a named stakeholder sign-off (Jasmijn: icon state change only, no message). Re-adding it means overriding that decision, not filling a gap. Get that confirmed before estimating.
3. If the toast is reinstated, the real work is **not** the toast call — it's a ~3-line swap to `handleAddToWishlist`. The cost sits in: (a) **no Zimmermann toast/alert theme recipe exists**, so it would ship as raw base Chakra unless one is built; (b) reinstating the "already in wishlist" branch that `handleAddToWishlistSilent` intentionally omits; (c) deciding whether remove-from-wishlist gets a matching message (currently silent, L620); (d) whether it also applies to the dead PLP handlers (`product-list/index.tsx` L1030), which already carry toasts but are unwired.
